frozen marsh pocket — SE flanking route

enemies.grid_notes: Ambush chief at the east road mouth (elev 3), behind the outcrop's shoulder — a forest-man who knows the levy's grain sledge is worth a winter. His scripted killing thrust at Grím (turn 4) is what falters.
On the SE frozen marsh (elev 0); circles the marsh ice to take the ford ramp from behind.
East outcrop crown (elev 4). Owns the crossing with bow range; the outcrop is the map's one climbable height and it is his.

East bank lip north of the road (elev 3), directly over the black drown hole at [9,3]. Cross-fire partner to e3; between them the ford is a killing lane until one lip is cleared. Shove him west and the river takes him.
Ice-runner on the mid-river plates north of the ford (elev 0); comfortable on slip tiles, herds the levy toward the drown holes.
Ice-runner on the plates south of the ford (elev 0); twin prong of e5.
Rear-block at the west road mouth (elev 1): steps onto the road behind the levy to close the retreat.

neutrals.grid_notes: Peddler, mid-crossing on the ford ice (elev 0) when the ambush springs; drags his pony E up the far road at 3-move. The battle's Sung/Unsung hinge and the Wyrd rumor's only carrier.
The pack-pony, one tile behind its master. Slips on ice; can block the very lane its master needs — cruel, teachable geometry.

objectives.primary: Break the ambush: fell the ambush chief (e1).
secondary: The peddler (n1) survives (whether he ESCAPES is left to the player's conscience).
No levy-man lost to a drown hole.
Clear one bank lip (e3 or e4 down) before turn 5.

triggers.note: Scripted: e1's charge reaches Grím and — nothing. His turn slips down the CT track (Slip preview, C-WYRD-01) with no VFX, no explanation; the log just reads wrong. DENIABLE (C-GRIM-05): ice underfoot, fog, luck. Post-battle script finalizes the flag true only if n1 escaped east; if n1 died or the battle went Unsung, the flag is cleared — nobody credible saw anything.
Survivors rout W into the fog; routers escaping make it Sung (C-ALIGN-04) even if the peddler drowned — a second, subtler hinge.
In fog, the valkyrie light is a smear. Beautiful and unverifiable — tone note for VFX.

designer_notes.height_gimmick: The only map where height is a weapon that points DOWN: bank lips overhang the ice by 2h (3h at e4's perch over the [9,3] hole). A shove or knockback off a 2h lip deals no fall damage (C-ELEV-01: falling >2h damages) — its payoff is the ice-slide in the push direction (slip tiles carry momentum) plus the plate-crack: any unit falling 2h+ onto a plate cracks it to water_shallow next tick. e4's 3h perch is the map's one damaging drop. Elevation here is never climbed for advantage; it is spent, by throwing people off it.
designer_notes.witness_setup: One peddler (n1) with a pack-pony is mid-crossing when the ambush springs; he flees east up the far road. The fog kills all other sightlines. If the player cuts him off on the ice, the fight vanishes into grey — Unsung, and Grím's flicker of impossible luck goes with it; if he escapes, 'the smith's boy the spears refuse' is talked into every hall by the Yule feast. The first Wyrd rumor is entirely the player's choice to permit (C-GRIM-05).
designer_notes.intent: River-crossing fight on slip tiles; teaches ice movement, knockback positioning, and drowning holes — the black water at [9,3] (under e4's lip; a 3h shove off [10,3] ends here) and at [6,5] (west ford mouth: row 6 is the true ramp lane, row 5 steps into the river) is water_deep terrain, intrinsically drowning-lethal with no drown_edge overlay needed (D-TERR-02) — and stages Grím's first involuntary Wyrd flicker as a scripted, deniable CT hiccup the fog half-swallows. CT-manipulation preview: the player SEES a turn slip on the timeline and is given no explanation.
